assessments.reasoning: Five contiguous captures cover bytes [0,73482) of SPDX’s commit-pinned json/details/GPL-2.0-or-later.json, reported SHA-256 9f8c6e6dc16cd05d9b9dc34ddd4a4e40df59f9813bae38d1f461ea245166fdf0. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 3 gives the exact ID, the distinguishing comment and the express recipient option. It cites GNU’s standalone HTML, OSI and OpenJDK. The generated text uses a Boston mailing address where the inspected GNU representation uses web addresses. The edition heading and substantive version option agree.

Capture 9c9c8acc5979433a89fc09b221f96ebf from the SPDX repository’s GitHub tag-object endpoint identifies v3.29.0 and its commit target 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48 in the cited range [336,540). This matches the generated later-option detail URL. GitHub records the tag as unsigned.

The FSF publisher capture matches the claim’s full edition digest. Section 9 explains who may elect a later version and which versions qualify. The post-terms sample gives the precise “at your option” language. It supports the meaning of the election when a holder adopts it for a work. The sample alone cannot establish adoption.

limitations: “Any later version” refers to later FSF-published GPL versions. Choosing a later version is optional. An unspecified version has a separate rule in §9.

As with the only claim, the notice condition is expressed in prose while the structured conditions array is empty. A crosswalk that consumes only the shared edition and key could incorrectly assign both elections to one file. Project-specific grants, modifications and exceptions require their own witnesses.
reasoning: SPDX 3.29.0 lists GPL-2.0-or-later. Its standard header says “either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” GPL §9 identifies the eligible later versions as those published by the Free Software Foundation. The claim accurately describes the recipient’s election when the applicable notice grants that choice.
